parsed.main_gap: Step 2 uses a false monotonicity inference, though the needed survival claim is immediately repairable from the move formula.

errors.description: A non-increasing positive integer can reach 1, so the stated reasoning does not prove that P remains greater than 1. Repair: each move leaves at least one selected replacement greater than 1—if gcd(m,n)>1 it survives, while if gcd(m,n)=1 then lcm(m,n)>1.
errors.quote: A positive integer that never increases and starts above $1$ can never reach $1$; hence $P > 1$ after any number of moves.

parsed.notes: The termination argument and prime-wise valuation invariant are correct. The only defect is a local false inference in Step 2; the write-up’s earlier summary states the correct replacement argument, and the repair is straightforward.
